How to do itHack Squat

Back on pad

Right
HIPS ON PAD
Wrong
HIPS OFF PAD

Right: Hips and lower back on the pad.

Wrong: Lower back rounded off the pad at the bottom.

Knee lockout

Right
SLIGHT BEND
Wrong
LOCKED

Right: Slight knee bend at the top.

Wrong: Knees locked at the top.

Upper and lower back and hips stay on the back pad.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Hips off padAt the bottom the hips and lower back lift off the back pad.
  2. Lower back roundsThe lower back rounds at the bottom of the squat.
Lower3 s
Push1 s
Hold1 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this mostly in the front of your thighs, and in your glutes.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansLower back lifting off the pad at the bottom.

    FixKeep your hips and back on the pad. Don't set your feet too high.

  • Usually meansYour feet are too close together.

    FixSet your feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Shoulders under the pads, back and hips on the pad.

  2. 2

    Feet shoulder-width, mid-plate, toes slightly out, knees in line with them.

  3. 3

    Hold the handles, don't push. Straighten up, release the safety.

  4. 4

    Don't stop short of parallel. Push up through your whole foot.

  5. 5

    Re-lock the safety to finish. Too heavy? Use the safety locks.

Risks and when to stop

  • Lifting your lower back off the pad can strain it.
  • Feet too close together can stress the knees.
  • Lower back or knee pain? This is usually not a good choice.

How to do itPendulum Squat

Heels flat

Right
HEELS FLAT
Wrong
HEELS LIFTED

Right: Heels flat at the bottom.

Wrong: Heels lifted off the platform.

Core braced, back pressed against the backrest.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Heels liftHeels lift off the platform at the bottom.
Lower3 s
Push1 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this mostly in the front of your thighs. Glutes and inner thighs help.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansKnees caving in or heels lifting puts strain on the knees.

    FixKeep knees over toes, whole foot down. Reduce the load if it persists.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the machine: shoulders under the pads, feet on the platform.

  2. 2

    Feet hip- to shoulder-width. Brace and press your back into the pad.

  3. 3

    Grip the handles firmly, then release the safety latch.

  4. 4

    Don't drop: lower over two to three seconds to at least parallel.

  5. 5

    Push up, torso upright. Extend fully without locking out hard.

Risks and when to stop

  • Knees caving in or heels lifting strains your knees.
  • Bouncing out of the bottom can cause injury.
  • Failed rep? Use the safety catch. To finish, lock it, check it holds.

How to do itLeg Extension

Knee lockout

Right
NOT LOCKED
Wrong
LOCKED

Right: Legs straight, knees not locked.

Wrong: Knees locked or hyperextended at the top.

Knees line up with the machine's pivot.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Back archesThe lower back arches as the legs extend.
  2. Back off padThe back lifts off the back pad.
Extend2 s
Hold1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your thighs.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansArching your lower back can lead to discomfort.

    FixBrace your abs. Keep your back pressed into the pad.

  • Usually meansFeeling it here, not in the quads, can mean a form error.

    FixStop if the pain is sharp. Reassess your form.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Knees at the pivot. Pad on your lower shins, just above ankles.

  2. 2

    Sit back against the pad, knees bent about 90 degrees.

  3. 3

    Hold the handles at your sides. Brace your abs.

  4. 4

    Breathe out and lift with your quads, don't kick. Pause briefly.

  5. 5

    Breathe in and lower slowly with control.

Risks and when to stop

  • Locking your knees at the top can add stress to the knee.
  • Arching your lower back can lead to discomfort.
  • Too much weight adds momentum and can increase the risk of injury.

How to do itLying Leg Curl

Hips on pad

Right
HIPS ON PAD
Wrong
HIPS LIFTING

Right: Front of the hips pressed into the pad.

Wrong: Hips lifting off the pad.

Line your knees up with the machine's axis.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Low back archesYour lower back arches as your legs curl.
Curl1 s
Hold1 s
Lower3 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the back of your thighs.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansArching the lower back can cause back pain and discomfort.

    FixBrace your abs. Use a lighter weight if your low back moves.

  • Usually meansSharp pain here is a reason to stop.

    FixStop the set. Try a lighter load or a different pad position.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Lie face down, knees near the bench edge, aligned with the axis.

  2. 2

    Roller on your lower calf, not pressing your heel or Achilles.

  3. 3

    Hold the handles, abs tight. Breathe out to curl, in to lower.

  4. 4

    Start knees nearly straight, not forced locked. Curl toward your glutes.

  5. 5

    Stop before your hips lift. Lower with control, stack never touching.

Risks and when to stop

  • Line your knees up with the machine's axis to prevent joint stress.
  • Arching your lower back can cause back pain and discomfort.
  • Sudden, jerking movements can lead to injury.

Knee steady

Right
KNEE IN PLACE
Wrong

Right: Knee stays in place as the leg curls.

Wrong: Knee travelling forward and back each rep.

Right
FOOT ABOVE KNEE

Tells
  1. Low back archesYour lower back arches as your leg curls.
Curl1 s
Hold1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the back of your thigh, strongest at the top.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansArching the lower back can cause back pain and discomfort.

    FixAvoid arching: contract your abs.

  • Usually meansPain here is a reason to stop.

    FixStop the set.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the pad just above the heel of your working leg.

  2. 2

    Thighs against the support pad. Hold the handles for balance.

  3. 3

    Plant your other foot firmly. Keep your upper body still.

  4. 4

    Curl until your foot is higher than your knee. Hold a second.

  5. 5

    Don't drop it: lower slowly, straighten fully. Finish one leg, then switch.

Risks and when to stop

  • Arching your lower back can cause back pain and discomfort.
  • Sudden, jerking movements can lead to injury.
  • Too much weight makes you use momentum and body swinging.

How to do itGlute Bridge

Spine at top

Right
STRAIGHT LINE
Wrong
BACK ARCHED

Right: Core tight, pelvis tucked, straight line at the top.

Wrong: Hips pushed too high, low back arched.

Keep the core tight and the pelvis tucked so the low back does not arch.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Back archedThe lower back overarches as the hips push too high.
Lift1 s
Hold1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your glutes and hamstrings.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansDriving through the toes makes the quads do more.

    FixPress through your heels.

  • Usually meansOverextending your back can lead to pain here.

    FixPull your belly button in and tuck your pelvis.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Lie on your back, feet flat, hip-width, knees in line with toes.

  2. 2

    Arms straight by your sides, or grip a barbell overhand.

  3. 3

    Pull your belly button in. Tuck your pelvis, low back flat.

  4. 4

    Exhale and drive with your hips, not your feet. Inhale to lower.

  5. 5

    Squeeze your glutes, hold the top for a second, lower slowly.

Risks and when to stop

  • Overextending your back can lead to lower back pain.
  • Pushing the hips too high increases the arch in your low back.
  • Back tension may mean wrong foot position or an overarched back.

How to do itCable Kickback

Braced back

Right
BACK FLAT
Wrong
BACK ARCHES

Right: Hinged forward, back flat, core braced.

Wrong: Lower back arching as the leg kicks back.

Brace so your lower back does not arch as the leg goes back.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Lower back archesYour lower back arches as the leg kicks back.
Kick back1 s
Hold1 s
Return2 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the glute of your working leg.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansPoor form can bring in the lower back.

    FixPull your belly button in and flatten your back.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the pulley lowest. Strap the cuff around your working ankle.

  2. 2

    Face and hold the machine. Hinge forward, weight on the other leg.

  3. 3

    Brace your trunk. Use your hands and free leg to stay still.

  4. 4

    Leg long, knee slightly bent. Hips level, toe pointing straight down.

  5. 5

    Drive back as far as you can. Squeeze, pause, return slowly.

Risks and when to stop

  • Heavy loading breaks your form down quickly on this long lever.
  • Can't lift without swinging the leg? Drop the weight.
  • Twisting your hips lifts the leg higher but makes it less effective.

How to do itResisted Hip Flexion

Upright torso

Right
STAND TALL
Wrong
LEANS BACK

Right: Torso upright, thigh at hip height.

Wrong: Torso leaning back, lower back arched.

Stand tall with the core braced and the standing leg steady.

Tells
  1. Leans backYou lean back to lift the leg higher.
  2. Lower back archesYour lower back arches as the knee comes up.
Lift2 s
Hold2 s

Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your hip and your lower belly.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansLeaning back or arching to lift higher.

    FixStand tall, core tight.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Strap the cuff to one ankle on a low cable.

  2. 2

    Face away from the machine, a little tension. Hold the frame.

  3. 3

    Brace your trunk, stand tall, hips level and square.

  4. 4

    Drive the knee straight up and forward, thigh about level. Don't swing.

  5. 5

    Pause briefly. Lower with control, never letting the stack slam. Switch legs.

Risks and when to stop

  • Arching the lower back to lift higher.
  • Acute hip or lower-back pain? Skip this exercise.
  • Stop if balance causes strain.
